nodes.text: Let $f$ be a random completely multiplicative function, where for each prime $p$ we independently choose $f(p)\in \{-1,1\}$ uniformly at random. Is it true that\[\limsup_{N\to \infty}\frac{\sum_{m\leq N}f(m)}{\sqrt{N}}=\infty\]with probability $1$?

#1144 : [Va99,1.11] number theory | probability This model of a random multiplicative function is sometimes called a Rademacher function, although this is sometimes reserved for a merely multiplicative function (which is $0$ on non-squarefree integers). See [520] for the partial sums of this alternative model. It should also be compared to another popular model of random completely multiplicative functions, Steinhaus functions, which have $f(p)$ uniformly distributed over the unit circle. Atherfold [At25] has proved that, almost surely,\[\sum_{m\leq N}f(m)\ll N^{1/2}(\log N)^{1+o(1)}.\] Additional thanks to : Adam Harper Proof expositions (0) If you would like to contribute an exposition of a proof related to this problem, please message a moderator or leave your exposition as a comment.
